# Brain Age {#sec-brainager}

This starter kit walks through the "Brain Age" outputs that have been derived from the anatomical scans. The examples in the kit rely on `bash` and `R`.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(dplyr)
library(fs)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
```
:::


Fundamentally, `brainager` calculations are about producing an estimated age based on measurable characteristics of a brain image, such as regional variations in gray matter density. The difference between estimated and chronological age is often referred to in the literature as the "brain age gap" (BAG) or "predicted age difference" (PAD), and is usually expressed as estimated minus chronological age. This value is often interpreted as an indicator of brain health, serving as a potential biomarker for neurodegenerative disease, cognitive decline, or general biological aging. For a comprehensive overview of Brain Age, see [Cole and Franke (2017)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5573489/) and the [brainageR GitHub Repository](https://github.com/james-cole/brainageR).

## Starting Project

### Locate data

We assume that the data were downloaded from the NIMH Data Archive (NDA) as a Data Package and saved to `{{< var nda.dir >}}` inside the project folder (@sec-nda describes what a package contains). Each NDA data structure is a table, `<structure>.txt`, and any files that the structure references are underneath a folder of the same name, `<structure>/`. Paths in the text start from the folder that holds the structure's files (for the MRI data, `<structure>/{{< var nda.prefix >}}`), while code chunks spell out the full path from the project folder.


The brain age estimates are referenced by `fmriresults01`, underneath `mris/derivatives/brainager`.

Most users will be interested in the predicted ages, which can be found in `sub-[recordid]/ses-[protocolid]/sub-[recordid]_ses-[protocolid]_T1w.tsv`. For example

```bash
$ cat sub-10003/ses-V1/sub-10003_ses-V1_T1w.tsv 
File    brain.predicted_age lower.CI    upper.CI
sub-10003_ses-V1_T1w    73.6037 72.9683 74.2392
```

Here is an example of how these files could be loaded using `R`.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# files referenced by fmriresults01 in the NDA package (see Locate Data)
fmriresults01 <- file.path(
  "data/nda/fmriresults01",
  "corral-secure/projects/A2CPS/products/consortium-data/pre-surgery"
)

# list all files
files <- dir_ls(
  file.path(fmriresults01, "mris/derivatives/brainager"),
  glob = "*T1w.tsv",
  recurse = TRUE
)

# read in all tsvs
ages <- read_tsv(files)
ages
```

## Considerations While Working on the Project

### Variability Across Scanners

Many MRI biomarkers exhibit variability across the scanners, which may confound some analyses. For an up-to-date assessment of the issue and overview of current thinking, please see @sec-mri-harmonization.


### Data Quality

As with any MRI derivative, all pipeline derivatives have been included. This means that products were included regardless of their quality, and so some products may have been generated from images that are known to have poor quality---rated "red", or incomparable. For details on the ratings and how to exclude them, see @sec-rawdata-mri-qc-joining. Additionally, extensive QC has not yet been performed on the derivatives themselves, and so there may be cases where pipelines produced atypical outputs. For an overview of planned checks, see [Confluence](https://a2cps.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DOC/pages/262471688/Image+Processing+Checks).


### Calculating the Brain Age Gap

Predicted ages are neat, but these values are most useful when compared against a participant's chronological age. These can be found in the `heal_demographics01` table of the NDA package, where `interview_age` is recorded in months.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
demo_file <- "data/nda/heal_demographics01.txt"

# line 2 of an NDA table describes each column, so take names from line 1 and data from line 3
baseline_ages <- read_tsv(
  demo_file,
  skip = 2,
  col_names = names(read_tsv(demo_file, n_max = 0, show_col_types = FALSE)),
  col_select = c("src_subject_id", "interview_age")
) |>
  transmute(record_id = as.integer(src_subject_id), age = interview_age / 12) |>
  distinct()

brainage <- ages_with_sub |>
  left_join(baseline_ages, by = join_by(sub == record_id)) |>
  mutate(brain_age_gap = brain.predicted_age - age) |>
  filter(!is.na(age)) # age not available for all participants
brainage
```

By plotting the predicted ages against the true ages, we can review the accuracy of the predictions.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
lm_eqn <- function(fit) {
  eq <- substitute(
    italic(y) == a + b %.% italic(age) * "," ~ ~ italic(r)^2 ~ "=" ~ r2,
    list(
      a = format(unname(coef(fit)[1]), digits = 2),
      b = format(unname(coef(fit)[2]), digits = 2),
      r2 = format(summary(fit)$r.squared, digits = 3)
    )
  )
  as.character(as.expression(eq))
}

fit <- lm(brain.predicted_age ~ age, data = brainage)

brainage |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = brain.predicted_age)) +
  geom_abline() +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x) +
  coord_fixed() +
  geom_text(x = 40, y = 80, label = lm_eqn(fit), parse = TRUE)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Predicted and Chronological Age. Each point corresponds to a participant.](brainager_files/figure-html/brainage-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


The "brain age gap" is the difference between predicted and true age. Positive gaps indicate "older" brains, and younger gaps indicate "younger" brains.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
brainage |>
  ggplot(aes(x = brain_age_gap)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  labs(x = "(<-- Younger) Brain Age Gap (Older -->)")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](brainager_files/figure-html/brainage-gap-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


### Correction

Note that using the raw Brain Age Gap can be problematic, and, for final analyses, it is typical to calculate a derivative that has been "corrected". The issue is that the predictions tend to be worse for the youngest and oldest people -- and so the gap is related to age (e.g., a relationship with larger raw gaps partly reflects a relationship with true age).


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
brainage |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = brain_age_gap)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x) +
  coord_fixed()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](brainager_files/figure-html/brainage-corrected-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


Corrections aim to make them independent, by, for example, residualizing. See @smith_estimation_2019.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
bag_age_fit <- lm(brain_age_gap ~ age, data = brainage)

brainage |>
  mutate(
    brain_age_gap_corrected = residuals(bag_age_fit),
    brain_age_gap = scale(brain_age_gap, scale = FALSE)
  ) |>
  select(sub, brain_age_gap, brain_age_gap_corrected) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = brain_age_gap, y = brain_age_gap_corrected)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](brainager_files/figure-html/brainage-fit-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


### Other Models

There are many models for calculating Brain Age. The values that have been pre-calculated for A2CPS are derived from a model that has been around for a while and used successfully in a variety of studies\ [@clausen_assessment_2022; @hobday_tissue_2022; @biondo_brain_2022]. For some analyses, it may be worthwhile to assess whether results persist across different models. For pain studies, one successful model has been DeepBrainNet\ [@valdes_brain_2023; @montesino_brain_2023; @bashyam_mri_2020], which can be used with derivatives from fMRIPrep.

### Methods

For additional documentation on the files and a detailed description of the methods, please see the official [brainageR repo](https://github.com/james-cole/brainageR).

It is in principle possible to replicate the processing that was used in a release by running the brainageR container[^docker] on the raw data. However, A2CPS Releases 1.0.0, 1.1.0, and 2.0.0 have not included raw T1w files for privacy reasons, and thus the end result may differ from the released version, which was generated on the raw images.

[^docker]: The container used by A2CPS is available [here](https://github.com/a2cps/mri_imaging_pipeline/blob/master/brainager_app/Dockerfile).
